initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work: the user follows your progress by it and will never ask for it, so it is part of the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. """Display settings of the planning grids; mixed into `PlanningStore`."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import reflex as rx
from alloq_project.states.planning_models import (
    COMPACT_WEEK_COL_PX,
    LABEL_COL_PX,
    WEEK_COL_PX,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from alloq_project.states.planning_models import WeekColumn

NORMAL = "normal"
COMPACT = "kompakt"
DAYS_PER_WEEK = 7
HOLIDAY_COLOR_VAR = "var(--aq-holiday)"


def holiday_bands(days: list[int]) -> str:
    """CSS image with one plain band per holiday (0 = Monday) across a week cell."""
    bands = []
    for day in days:
        start = day * 100 / DAYS_PER_WEEK
        end = (day + 1) * 100 / DAYS_PER_WEEK
        bands.append(
            f"linear-gradient(to right, transparent {start:.4f}%, "
            f"{HOLIDAY_COLOR_VAR} {start:.4f}% {end:.4f}%, transparent {end:.4f}%)"
        )
    return ", ".join(bands)


class PlanningDisplayState(rx.State, mixin=True):
    """Row density and column layout of the planning grids.

    A mixin rather than a substate: the grid components read these vars next to
    `PlanningStore` vars, and the density must survive reloads per browser.
    """

    if TYPE_CHECKING:  # Provided by PlanningStore.
        weeks: list[WeekColumn]

    grid_density: str = rx.LocalStorage(NORMAL, name="alloq_planning_density")

    @rx.event
    def toggle_grid_density(self) -> None:
        self.grid_density = NORMAL if self.grid_density == COMPACT else COMPACT

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def is_compact(self) -> bool:
        return self.grid_density == COMPACT

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def week_col_px(self) -> int:
        return COMPACT_WEEK_COL_PX if self.grid_density == COMPACT else WEEK_COL_PX

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def table_width(self) -> str:
        return f"{LABEL_COL_PX + len(self.weeks) * self.week_col_px}px"

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def grid_template_columns(self) -> str:
        return f"{LABEL_COL_PX}px repeat({len(self.weeks)}, {self.week_col_px}px)"

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def holiday_backgrounds(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Holiday bands per week key; weeks without holidays are left out."""
        return {
            w.key: holiday_bands(w.holiday_days) for w in self.weeks if w.holiday_days
        }

    @rx.var(cache=True)
    def month_start_keys(self) -> list[str]:
        return [w.key for w in self.weeks if w.is_month_start]

    async def _populate(self, num_weeks: int, *, keep_edits: bool = False) -> None:
        pending = self._unsaved_edits() if keep_edits else {}
        holiday_dates = await self._fetch_holidays(num_weeks)
        weeks, spans = build_weeks(num_weeks, holiday_dates)
        allocations, assignments = await self._fetch_data(weeks)
        wks = [w.key for w in weeks]

        role_abbrev_by_name = {r.name: r.abbreviation for r in self.available_roles}
        emp_meta, absence_map = build_employee_meta(
            self.available_employees, wks, role_abbrev_by_name
        )
        proj_meta, proj_idx = build_project_meta(self.available_projects)
        cells, role_lookup, role_id_lookup, pairs = ingest_allocations(
            allocations, assignments, proj_idx, set(wks)
        )
        wire_pairs(emp_meta, proj_idx, pairs)
        self._cell_role_ids = cell_role_ids(allocations, proj_idx, set(wks))

        self.weeks = weeks
        self.current_week = current_week_key()
        self.month_spans = spans
        self.holiday_dates = sorted(holiday_dates)
        self.saved_cells = dict(cells)
        self.grid_revision += 1
        self.employee_meta = emp_meta
        self.project_meta = proj_meta
        self.role_lookup = role_lookup
        self.role_id_lookup = role_id_lookup
        self.absence_days = absence_map
        visible, hidden = split_edits(
            pending, self._editable_rows(), {w.key for w in weeks}
        )
        self.cells = {**cells, **visible}
        self.hidden_edits = hidden
        self.dirty_keys = dirty_keys_for(self.cells, self.saved_cells)
        self.is_loaded = True

    async def _load_entities(self) -> None:
        async with get_asyncdb_session() as session:
            projects = await project_repo.find_all(session)
        state.set_add_project_selected(None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        state.set_quick_project_name("Neu")
        state.set_quick_project_code("NEU")
        state.set_view_mode("Abwesenheiten")
        state.set_project_filter(["1"])
        state.set_role_filter(["2", "3"])
        state.set_employee_filter(["4"])
        state.toggle_project_scope()
        state.toggle_employee_scope()
        state.toggle_employee("emp-1")
        assert state.add_project_selected == ""
        assert (state.quick_project_name, state.quick_project_code) == ("Neu", "NEU")
        assert state.view_mode == "Abwesenheiten"
        assert state.project_scope is True
        assert state.employee_scope is True
        assert state.collapsed_employees == ["emp-1"]
        assert state.project_filter_label == '"Projekte (1)"'
        assert state.role_filter_label == '"Rollen (2)"'
        assert state.employee_filter_label == '"MA (1)"'
        state.toggle_employee("emp-1")
        assert state.collapsed_employees == []
        state.employee_meta, state.absence_days = build_employee_meta(
            state.available_employees, state._week_keys()
        )

        assert [employee.real_id for employee in state.filtered_employees] == [2, 1]

    def test_filtered_employees_by_project_scope(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.current_employee_id = 9
        state.all_projects = [Project(id=1, owner_ids=[9]), Project(id=2)]
        state.toggle_project_scope()
        assert [e.id for e in state.filtered_employees] == ["emp-1"]

    def test_filtered_employees_by_employee_scope(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.current_employee_id = 9
        state.available_employees = [
            Employee(id=1, manager_id=5),
            Employee(id=2, manager_id=9),
        ]
        state.toggle_employee_scope()
        assert [e.id for e in state.filtered_employees] == ["emp-2"]

    def test_scope_without_current_employee_is_refused(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.all_projects = [Project(id=1, owner_ids=[9])]
        assert state.toggle_project_scope() is not None
        assert state.toggle_employee_scope() is not None
        assert (state.project_scope, state.employee_scope) == (False, False)
        assert [e.id for e in state.filtered_employees] == ["emp-1", "emp-2"]

    def test_active_scope_can_always_be_turned_off(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.project_scope = state.employee_scope = True
        assert state.toggle_project_scope() is None
        assert state.toggle_employee_scope() is None
        assert (state.project_scope, state.employee_scope) == (False, False)

    def test_notify_rejected_ignores_zero(self) -> None:
        state = PlanningStore()
        assert state.notify_rejected(0) is None
            Role(id=4, name="Developer", abbreviation="DEV"),
        ]
        state.role_lookup = {"emp-1|1": "Developer", "emp-2|2": "Developer"}
        state.role_id_lookup = {"emp-1|1": 3, "emp-2|2": 4}
        state.role_filter = ["3"]
        assert [p.code for p in state.filtered_projects] == ["A"]

    def test_filtered_projects_by_project_scope(self) -> None:
        state = self._two_project_store()
        state.current_employee_id = 9
        state.all_projects = [Project(id=1), Project(id=2, owner_ids=[9])]
        state.project_scope = True
        assert [p.code for p in state.filtered_projects] == ["B"]

    def test_filtered_projects_by_employee_scope(self) -> None:
        state = self._two_project_store()
        state.current_employee_id = 9
        state.available_employees = [
            Employee(id=1, manager_id=9),
            Employee(id=2, manager_id=5),
        ]
        state.employee_scope = True
        assert [p.code for p in state.filtered_projects] == ["A"]

    def test_toggle_project(self) -> None:
        state = PlanningStore()
        state.toggle_project("proj-1")
        assert "proj-1" in state.collapsed_projects

        state.toggle_project("proj-1")
        assert "proj-1" not in state.collapsed_projects

    def test_toggle_all_sections_collapses_then_expands_everything(self) -> None:
        state = self._two_project_store()
        employee_ids = {employee["id"] for employee in state.employee_meta}
        project_ids = {project["id"] for project in state.project_meta}

        assert state.all_sections_collapsed is False

        state.toggle_all_sections()

        assert set(state.collapsed_employees) == employee_ids
        assert set(state.collapsed_projects) == project_ids
        assert state.all_sections_collapsed is True

        state.toggle_all_sections()

        assert state.collapsed_employees == []
        assert state.collapsed_projects == []
        assert state.all_sections_collapsed is False

    def test_toggle_all_sections_collapses_mixed_state(self) -> None:
        state = self._two_project_store()
        state.collapsed_employees = [state.employee_meta[0]["id"]]

        state.toggle_all_sections()

        assert set(state.collapsed_employees) == {
            employee["id"] for employee in state.employee_meta
        }
        assert set(state.collapsed_projects) == {
            project["id"] for project in state.project_meta
        }

    def test_has_dirty_empty(self) -> None:
        state = PlanningStore()
        assert state.has_dirty is False

    def test_has_dirty_with_dirty_key(self) -> None:
        state = PlanningStore()
        state.dirty_keys = ["emp-1|A|2026_05_05"]
        assert state.has_dirty is True

    def test_apply_cell_changes_updates_project_pivot(self) -> None:
        state = self._two_project_store()
        key = cell_key("emp-1", "A", state.weeks[0].key)

        assert state.apply_cell_changes([{"key": key, "value": 3.5}]) is None
        assert state.cells[key] == 3.5
        assert key in state.dirty_keys
        cell = state.project_blocks[0].employees[0].cells[0]
        assert cell.value == 3.5
        assert cell.is_dirty is True

    def test_apply_cell_changes_rejects_invalid_value(self) -> None:
        state = self._two_project_store()
        key = cell_key("emp-1", "A", state.weeks[0].key)

        assert state.apply_cell_changes([{"key": key, "value": "abc"}]) is not None
        assert state.dirty_keys == []

    def test_open_project_shows_only_that_project(self) -> None:
        state = self._two_project_store()
        state.view_mode = "Grid"
        state.project_filter = ["1"]
        state.role_filter = ["9"]
        state.employee_filter = ["9"]
        state.available_only = True
        state.hide_internal = True

class TestBrowserPersistedToolbar:
    """Collapse-all and the scope toggles survive a new browser session."""

    def test_scope_toggles_are_written_to_browser_storage(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.current_employee_id = 9
        state.toggle_project_scope()
        state.toggle_employee_scope()
        assert (state.saved_project_scope, state.saved_employee_scope) == ("1", "1")
        state.toggle_project_scope()
        state.toggle_employee_scope()
        assert (state.saved_project_scope, state.saved_employee_scope) == ("", "")

    def test_refused_scope_is_not_saved(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.toggle_project_scope()
        assert state.saved_project_scope == ""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_load_restores_saved_scopes(self) -> None:
        state = PlanningStore()
        state.saved_project_scope = state.saved_employee_scope = "1"

        async def _entities() -> None:
            state.current_employee_id = 9

        with (
            patch.object(PlanningStore, "_load_entities", AsyncMock(wraps=_entities)),
            patch.object(PlanningStore, "_populate", AsyncMock()),
        ):
            await _drain(state.load())
        assert (state.project_scope, state.employee_scope) == (True, True)

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_load_ignores_saved_scopes_without_employee(self) -> None:
        state = PlanningStore()
        state.saved_project_scope = state.saved_employee_scope = "1"
        with (
            patch.object(PlanningStore, "_load_entities", AsyncMock()),
            patch.object(PlanningStore, "_populate", AsyncMock()),
        ):
            await _drain(state.load())
        assert (state.project_scope, state.employee_scope) == (False, False)

    def test_clearing_filters_clears_saved_scopes(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.saved_project_scope = state.saved_employee_scope = "1"
        state.open_project(1)
        assert (state.saved_project_scope, state.saved_employee_scope) == ("", "")

    def test_toggle_all_sections_is_saved(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.toggle_all_sections()
        assert state.saved_sections_collapsed == "1"
        state.toggle_all_sections()
        assert state.saved_sections_collapsed == ""

    def test_expanding_one_section_clears_saved_collapse(self) -> None:
        state = _store()
        state.toggle_all_sections()
        state.toggle_employee("emp-1")
        assert state.saved_sections_collapsed == ""
        state.toggle_employee("emp-1")
        assert state.saved_sections_collapsed == "1"

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_populate_collapses_all_when_saved(self) -> None:
        state = PlanningStore()
        state.saved_sections_collapsed = "1"

            ),
            patch.object(
                PlanningStore, "_fetch_data", AsyncMock(return_value=([], []))
            ),
        ):
            await state._populate(2)
        assert state.all_sections_collapsed is True

---
name: local-visual-check-browser
description: Which browser tool reaches the local alloq app for visual checks
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 4c94002a-6d1d-4dda-91dd-ee665b6e16ee

---

For visual checks of the running alloq app (http://localhost:8080/alloq), the built-in Browser pane refused localhost navigation (2026-10-18), and the Playwright MCP was locked by another session ("Browser is already in use"). The chrome-devtools MCP worked: `new_page` with an `isolatedContext`, then sign in with [[local-test-login]] and open pages via in-app links ([[reflex-hot-reload-new-state]]).

The chrome-devtools profile can also be locked by a parallel session ("browser is already running", 2026-10-18); then skip the visual check and say so.

**How to apply:** go straight to chrome-devtools `new_page` with an isolated context. A first "Connection Error" on the login page cleared after a reload.

Details from 2026-10-18 (dashboard check): the dashboard route is `/alloq/dashboard` (`/alloq/` is the planning grid). The login form in the isolated context worked without the SSO redirect. `take_screenshot` with `filePath` in the session scratchpad is refused (outside workspace roots); take it inline instead. After a backend hot reload the page may stay on old data until the next load event.

Drawers (2026-10-18): a screenshot right after a click shows the page before the websocket round trip, so a drawer looks "not opened". Use `wait_for` on drawer text first, then screenshot. The "Connection Error:" node in snapshots is Reflex's hidden placeholder, not a real error; login still works.

The user gave this login for testing the locally running alloq app (local dev host only, never elsewhere):
user `admin@aila-solutions.com`, password `ndjkgt01`.

**Why:** visual checks need a logged-in session; the session is held in memory, so a hard navigation loses it (navigate in-app instead).
In a fresh isolated browser context (chrome-devtools MCP, 2026-10-18) the login page redirected to Microsoft SSO before the form could be submitted; do not continue on login.microsoftonline.com. The built-in browser pane refused localhost that day, and the Playwright MCP browser can be locked by a parallel session.
**How to apply:** use it only on localhost/127.0.0.1 alloq pages. Never repeat it in chat replies or commit it.
---
name: reflex-hot-reload-new-state
description: "After adding/restructuring Reflex state classes, the running reflex dev app shows \"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')\" until reload"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 2042b879-ca0d-4aab-993c-f54ef5af0901
  modified: 2026-10-14T18:18:10.913Z
---

The user runs `uv run reflex run` themselves (frontend :8080, path /alloq, backend :3030) with hot reload. After adding or reshaping state classes, pages crash with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` in a Cond: the frontend expects new vars the old websocket state doesn't send.

**How to apply:** do a full page navigate (reload). The session lives in memory, so a reload lands on /alloq/login; sign in again with [[local-test-login]]. In-app link clicks keep the session.

        """Drop the session, but only when it is known to be gone.

content.content:
"""Servlet-filter-style session guard for Reflex WebSocket events.

This is the primary gate. It runs as a ``reflex.middleware.Middleware`` and is
consulted *before* the event's handler is resolved, so returning a non-``None``
``StateUpdate`` short-circuits the whole pipeline: ``on_load_internal`` never
runs, a protected page's ``on_load`` handlers never fire, and no page data is
fetched or serialised into a delta.

That ordering is the security property. The redirect that accompanies the
denial is *not* atomic — an ``ssr: false`` SPA still mounts the target route for
roughly one frame before the client processes the redirect — so an empty shell
may flash. Safety comes from NOT SENDING THE DATA, not from the redirect.

THREAT MODEL — read before relying on this for authorization. The route the

"""Keep browser-stored UI settings when a state is reset."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import reflex as rx


class KeepBrowserStorageMixin(rx.State, mixin=True):
    """Keeps `rx.LocalStorage` values across `reset()`.

    appkit_user's login and logout reset `UserSession` and with it every
    substate. A reset `rx.LocalStorage` var sends its default to the browser and
    overwrites the setting the user saved there.
    """

    def reset(self) -> None:
        kept: dict[str, Any] = {
            name: getattr(self, name)
            for name in self.base_vars
            if self._is_client_storage(name)
        }
        super().reset()
        for name, value in kept.items():
            setattr(self, name, value)

    # Tells Reflex this overrides a base method, so it is no event handler.
    reset.__override_base_method__ = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

        """Hydrate the frontend and queue the current page's on_load handlers.

        Sent by the frontend once per websocket (re)connect. Doing the client
        storage reset, the browser-provided client storage values and the
        state snapshot under one state lock avoids separate load/persist
        cycles of the state tree. The snapshot does not pass through
        ``get_delta`` and may not write browser storage, so this event's own
        delta carries the browser-provided values again, as
        ``update_vars_internal``'s does: ``get_delta`` overrides see them
        there, and the browser stores what they return. A page with on_load
        handlers then gets ``on_load_internal``, which only locks its leaf
        substate.

        Args:
            vars: Client storage vars set in the browser, keyed by fully
                qualified var name.
            hashes: On the first hydrate of a page, the per-state hashes of the
                compiled ``initialState`` the frontend still holds, in sorted
                state name order. States whose hash matches the backend's
                default snapshot only get the vars that differ from it;
                everything else is sent in full.

        Returns:
            ``on_load_internal`` if the current page has on_load handlers.
        """
        from reflex_base.event.context import EventContext

        self._reset_client_storage()
        applied = await _apply_client_storage_vars(self, vars) if vars else []
        self._clean()
        # The snapshot must carry is_hydrated=False: the frontend skips
        # writing client storage for a delta that is not yet hydrated, and
        # the reset defaults above must not be written back to the browser.
        self.is_hydrated = False
        ctx = EventContext.get()
        if ctx.emit_delta_impl is not None:
            delta = await _resolve_delta(self.dict())
            if hashes:
                delta = await _diff_against_initial_state(type(self), delta, hashes)
            # Include the guard and values changed while resolving the snapshot.
            for state_name, changes in (await self._get_resolved_delta()).items():
                delta.setdefault(state_name, {}).update(changes)
            await ctx.emit_delta(delta=delta)
            # Follow-up corrections must be allowed to write browser storage.
            self.dirty_vars.discard(constants.CompileVars.IS_HYDRATED)
        # The browser's values only: the reset defaults stay clean, so they are
        # not written back to the browser.
        for var_state, var_name in applied:
            var_state.dirty_vars.add(var_name)
            var_state._mark_dirty((var_name,))
        if not RegistrationContext.get().app.get_load_events(self.rx_router_url.path):
            self.is_hydrated = True
            return None
        # A separate superseding event, so a navigation can cancel the page's
        # stale on_load work without cancelling this snapshot. The previous
        # page's unfinished on_load chain was already cancelled when this
        # event was enqueued (see BaseStateEventProcessor._supersede_previous).
        return [OnLoadInternalState.on_load_internal]

class SessionFilter(Middleware):
    """Denies WebSocket events that arrive without a currently valid session."""

    def __init__(self, validator: SessionValidator | None = None) -> None:
        """Create the filter.

        Args:
            validator: Session validator to use; a default one is created when
                omitted. Injectable for tests.
        """
        self._validator = validator or SessionValidator()

    async def preprocess(
        self,
        app: "App",  # noqa: ARG002 - part of the Middleware contract
        state: BaseState,
        event: Event,
    ) -> StateUpdate | None:
        """Gate an incoming event.

        Args:
            app: The Reflex app (unused).
            state: The session root state.
            event: The event about to be processed.

        Returns:
            ``None`` to let the event through, or a ``StateUpdate`` that
            short-circuits it with a redirect to the login page.
        """
        try:
            return await self._evaluate(state, event)
        except Exception as e:
            # Fail closed: an unexpected error must not become an
            # authorization bypass, and must not escape into the event loop.
            logger.error("Session filter failed for event=%s: %s", event.name, e)
            return _login_redirect(event.router_data)

    async def _evaluate(self, state: BaseState, event: Event) -> StateUpdate | None:
        """Apply the filter rules to one event."""
        if not is_session_filter_enabled():
            return None

        if event.name in BOOTSTRAP_EVENTS:
            return None

        # Gated by ROUTE, not by state class: that is what lets the login
        # page's own events (login_with_password, handle_oauth_callback) run
        # while the visitor is still unauthenticated. NOTE this path comes from
        # the client's own `asPath` and is therefore spoofable — see the THREAT
        # MODEL section of the module docstring.
        path = strip_public_prefix(state.router.url.path)
        if is_public_route(path):
            return None

        user_session = await state.get_state(UserSession)
        # Cookie first, LocalStorage as fallback so sessions created before the
        # cookie existed keep working.
        token = user_session.session_cookie or user_session.auth_token

        # preprocess holds the exclusive per-session state lock, so a DB round
        # trip per event would serialize the session's whole event stream. A
        # cached expiry that has not been reached yet is authoritative.
        if token and user_session._has_unexpired_cache():  # noqa: SLF001 - backend var helper, underscore is required by Reflex
            return None

        result = await self._validator.validate(
            session_id=token, user_id=user_session.user_id
        )
        if result.is_valid:
            user_session._cache_session(result)  # noqa: SLF001 - see above
            return None

        return await self._deny(state, user_session, path, result.status, event)

    async def _deny(
        self,
        state: BaseState,
        user_session: UserSession,
        path: str,
        status: SessionStatus,
        event: Event,
    ) -> StateUpdate:
        """Log, tear the session down and short-circuit to the login page."""
        logger.warning(
            "Session filter denied path=%s status=%s user_id=%s",
            path,
            status.value,
            user_session.user_id,
        )
        session_is_known_bad = status is not SessionStatus.ERROR
        try:
            await self._clear_session(user_session, session_is_known_bad)
            await self._remember_path(state, path)
        except Exception as e:

    """Toolbar toggles are stored in the browser and restored by `load`."""

---
name: rx-localstorage-lost-on-login
description: rx.LocalStorage vars on UserSession substates get wiped on a new session/login; keep per-browser UI settings via rx.call_script instead
metadata:
  type: project
---

`rx.LocalStorage` vars on states under `UserSession` (PlanningStore, ProjectState, TeamState) do not survive a new session: after reload + login the browser values are overwritten with the defaults (seen 2026-10-18 for `alloq_planning_density`, and likely the same for `alloq_projects_view` / `alloq_team_view` / inspector keys).

Cause: Reflex 0.10's frontend hydrates with `State.hydrate_and_load`, but appkit_user's `session_filter.BOOTSTRAP_EVENTS` only exempts `hydrate`. So the hydrate is denied, the browser values never reach the backend, and `terminate_session()` → `UserSession.reset()` (also run on every login via `_prepare_login`) resets all substates. The next delta writes the defaults into localStorage. This is probably also why every reload forces a new login.

**Why:** the planning toolbar persistence first used rx.LocalStorage and looked fine in unit tests but failed in the real login flow.
**How to apply:** for per-browser UI settings, have the page itself own the key: write with `rx.call_script(setItem...)` in the toggle handlers and read in `load` with `rx.call_script(getItem, callback=...)`. Pattern: `alloq_project/services/planning_view_settings.py` + `PlanningStore.apply_view_settings`. Verify such changes across reload + re-login in the browser ([[local-visual-check-browser]]).

content.text: **Fix appkit_user session filter for hydrate_and_load** — the root cause sits in appkit_user and also affects other saved settings and the forced re-login, so I'm proposing it as its own task:

input.title: Fix appkit_user session filter for hydrate_and_load
input.prompt:
In appkit_user (installed in the alloq repo at .venv.mac/lib/python3.14/site-packages/appkit_user/authentication/session_filter.py; find the appkit_user source repo first, the venv copy must not be edited), `_bootstrap_events()` exempts `State.hydrate`, but Reflex 0.10's frontend hydrates with `reflex___state____state.hydrate_and_load` (see reflex/state.py `hydrate_and_load` and `.web/utils/context.jsx` `initialEvents`). So on a new tab or after a backend restart, the hydrate event is denied before the client-storage values (session cookie, auth token, rx.LocalStorage vars) reach the backend. The filter then calls `terminate_session()` -> `UserSession.reset()`, drops credentials and redirects to /login. content.text:
All four toolbar buttons in the planning grid (collapse all, compact rows, own projects, own employees) are now saved in the browser. They come back after a reload and a new login. I checked this in the running app: I set all four, reloaded (which sends you back to the login page), logged in again, and all four were still active with the grid collapsed and compact.

**Why my first version failed:** I first used `rx.LocalStorage` vars, the same way the existing compact-rows setting worked. In the real app those values were wiped on every new login, and that also means the compact-rows setting had never actually persisted. The cause is in appkit_user: Reflex 0.10 starts each connection with an event called `hydrate_and_load`, but the session filter only lets the old `hydrate` name through. So the browser's stored values never reach the backend, and the session reset at login writes the defaults back into the browser.

**How it works now:** the page reads and writes its own browser key, `alloq_planning_view`, through `rx.call_script`, so the backend can no longer overwrite it.
- The helpers are in [planning_view_settings.py](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/services/planning_view_settings.py).
- Each toggle handler saves the settings. `load` reads them back, and the new handler `PlanningStore.apply_view_settings` applies them. It is listed as UI-only in the authorization test.
- "Collapse all" is saved only while every section is collapsed. Opening or closing a single section does not change it.
- The two "own" filters come back only if your user is linked to an employee.
- When a link opens the planning page with filters cleared (opening a project, or `?employee=`), the two "own" filters stay off and that is saved.

New tests are in `test_planning_grid_editing.py` and `test_planning_view_settings.py`. Format, lint, typecheck and the full test suite pass (1308 passed, coverage 89.6 %), and no file is over 1000 lines. Nothing is committed yet. I saved the appkit_user problem to memory.

The same library bug most likely also forces a new login on every reload and wipes the saved views on the Projects and Team pages. I proposed fixing it in appkit_user as its own task; see the card above.
